In [[mathematics]], a '''Sobolev mapping''' is a mapping between [[manifold]]s which has [[smoothness]] in some sense. 
Sobolev mappings appear naturally in manifold-constrained problems in the [[calculus of variations]] and [[partial differential equation]]s, including the theory of [[harmonic map]]s.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hélein |first1=Frédéric |last2=Wood |first2=John C. |title=Harmonic maps |journal=Handbook of Global Analysis |date=2008 |pages=417–491 |doi=10.1016/B978-044452833-9.50009-7|isbn=978-0-444-52833-9 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Eells |first1=J. |last2=Lemaire |first2=L. |title=A Report on Harmonic Maps |journal=Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society |date=March 1978 |volume=10 |issue=1 |pages=1–68 |doi=10.1112/blms/10.1.1}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Eells |first1=J. |last2=Lemaire |first2=L. |title=Another Report on Harmonic Maps |journal=Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society |date=September 1988 |volume=20 |issue=5 |pages=385–524 |doi=10.1112/blms/20.5.385}}</ref>

== Definition ==

Given [[Riemannian manifold]]s <math>M</math> and <math>N</math>, which is assumed by [[Nash embedding theorems|Nash's smooth embedding theorem]] [[without loss of generality]] to be [[Isometric embedding|isometrically embedded]] into <math>\mathbb{R}^\nu</math> as <ref>{{cite journal |last1=Mironescu |first1=Petru |title=Sobolev maps on manifolds: degree, approximation, lifting |journal=Contemporary Mathematics |date=2007 |volume=446 |pages=413–436 |doi=10.1090/conm/446/08642|isbn=9780821841907 |url=https://hal.archives-ouvertes.fr/hal-00747679/file/sobolev_spaces_survey_20070120.pdf }}</ref><ref name="Hang_Lin_2003" >{{cite journal |last1=Hang |first1=Fengbo |last2=Lin |first2=Fanghua |title=Topology of sobolev mappings, II |journal=Acta Mathematica |date=2003 |volume=191 |issue=1 |pages=55–107 |doi=10.1007/BF02392696|s2cid=121520479 |doi-access=free }}</ref>
<math display="block">
 W^{s, p} (M, N)
 :=
\{u \in W^{s, p} (M, \mathbb{R}^\nu) \, \vert \, u (x) \in N \text{ for almost every } x \in M\}.
</math>
First-order (<math>s=1</math>) Sobolev mappings can also be defined in the context of [[metric space]]s.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Chiron |first1=David |title=On the definitions of Sobolev and BV spaces into singular spaces and the trace problem|journal=Communications in Contemporary Mathematics |date=August 2007 |volume=09 |issue=4 |pages=473–513 |doi=10.1142/S0219199707002502|url=https://hal.science/hal-00809291 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Hajłasz |first1=Piotr |chapter=Sobolev Mappings between Manifolds and Metric Spaces |title=Sobolev Spaces in Mathematics I |series=International Mathematical Series |date=2009 |volume=8 |pages=185–222 |doi=10.1007/978-0-387-85648-3_7|isbn=978-0-387-85647-6 }}</ref>

== Approximation ==

The strong approximation problem consists in determining whether smooth mappings from <math>M</math> to <math>N</math> are dense in <math>W^{s, p} (M, N)</math> with respect to the norm topology.
When <math>sp > \dim M</math>, [[Morrey's inequality]] implies that Sobolev mappings are continuous and can thus be strongly approximated by smooth maps.
When <math>sp = \dim M</math>, Sobolev mappings have [[vanishing mean oscillation]]<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Brezis |first1=H. |author-link=Haïm Brezis |last2=Nirenberg |first2=L. |author-link2=Louis Nirenberg |title=Degree theory and BMO; part I: Compact manifolds without boundaries |journal=Selecta Mathematica |date=September 1995 |volume=1 |issue=2 |pages=197–263 |doi=10.1007/BF01671566|s2cid=195270732 }}</ref> and can thus be approximated by smooth maps.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Schoen |first1=Richard |author-link=Richard Schoen |last2=Uhlenbeck |first2=Karen |author-link2=Karen Uhlenbeck |title=A regularity theory for harmonic maps |journal=Journal of Differential Geometry |date=1 January 1982 |volume=17 |issue=2 |doi=10.4310/jdg/1214436923|doi-access=free }}</ref>

When <math>sp <\dim M</math>, the question of density is related to [[obstruction theory]]:
<math>C^\infty (M, N)</math> is dense in <math>W^{1, p} (M, N)</math> [[if and only if]] every continuous mapping on a from a <math>\lfloor p\rfloor</math>–dimensional [[Triangulation (topology)|triangulation]] of <math>M</math> into <math>N</math> is the restriction of a continuous map from <math>M</math> to <math>N</math>.<ref name="Bethuel_1991">{{cite journal |last1=Bethuel |first1=Fabrice |title=The approximation problem for Sobolev maps between two manifolds |journal=Acta Mathematica |date=1991 |volume=167 |pages=153–206 |doi=10.1007/BF02392449|s2cid=122996551 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name="Hang_Lin_2003" />

The problem of finding a sequence of weak approximation of maps in <math>W^{1, p} (M, N)</math> is equivalent to the strong approximation when <math>p</math> is not an [[integer]].<ref name="Bethuel_1991" />
When <math>p</math> is an integer, a necessary condition is that the restriction to a <math>\lfloor p - 1\rfloor</math>-dimensional triangulation of every continuous mapping from a <math>\lfloor p\rfloor</math>–dimensional triangulation of <math>M</math> into <math>N</math> coincides with the restriction a continuous map from <math>M</math> to <math>N</math>.<ref name="Hang_Lin_2003" />
When <math>p = 2</math>, this condition is sufficient.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Pakzad |first1=M.R. |last2=Rivière |first2=T. |title=Weak density of smooth maps for the Dirichlet energy between manifolds |journal=Geometric and Functional Analysis |date=February 2003 |volume=13 |issue=1 |pages=223–257 |doi=10.1007/s000390300006|s2cid=121794503 }}</ref> 
For <math>W^{1, 3} (M, \mathbb{S}^2)</math> with <math>\dim M \ge 4</math>, this condition is not sufficient.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bethuel |first1=Fabrice |title=A counterexample to the weak density of smooth maps between manifolds in Sobolev spaces |journal=Inventiones Mathematicae |date=February 2020 |volume=219 |issue=2 |pages=507–651 |doi=10.1007/s00222-019-00911-3|arxiv=1401.1649 |bibcode=2020InMat.219..507B |s2cid=119627475 }}</ref>

== Homotopy ==

The homotopy problem consists in describing and classifying the [[path-connected]] components of the space <math>W^{s, p}(M, N)</math> endowed with the norm topology.
When <math>0 < s \le 1</math> and <math>\dim M \le sp</math>, then the path-connected components of <math>W^{s, p} (M, N)</math> are essentially the same as the path-connected components of <math>C(M, N)</math>: two maps in <math>W^{s, p} (M, N) \cap C (M, N)</math> are connected by a path in <math>W^{s, p} (M, N)</math> if and only if they are connected by a path in <math>C(M, N)</math>, any path-connected component of <math>W^{s, p} (M, N)</math> and any path-connected component of <math>C (M, N)</math> intersects <math>W^{s, p} (M, N) \cap C (M, N)</math> non trivially.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Brezis |first1=Haı̈m |last2=Li |first2=YanYan |title=Topology and Sobolev spaces |journal=Comptes Rendus de l'Académie des Sciences - Series I - Mathematics |date=September 2000 |volume=331 |issue=5 |pages=365–370 |doi=10.1016/S0764-4442(00)01656-6|bibcode=2000CRASM.331..365B }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Brezis |first1=Haim |last2=Li |first2=Yanyan |title=Topology and Sobolev Spaces |journal=Journal of Functional Analysis |date=July 2001 |volume=183 |issue=2 |pages=321–369 |doi=10.1006/jfan.2000.3736|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bousquet |first1=Pierre |title=Fractional Sobolev spaces and topology |journal=Nonlinear Analysis: Theory, Methods & Applications |date=February 2008 |volume=68 |issue=4 |pages=804–827 |doi=10.1016/j.na.2006.11.038}}</ref>
When <math>\dim M > p</math>, two maps in <math>W^{1, p} (M, N)</math> are connected by a continuous path in <math>W^{1, p} (M, N)</math> if and only if their restrictions to a generic <math>\lfloor p - 1\rfloor</math>-dimensional triangulation are homotopic.<ref name="Hang_Lin_2003" />{{rp|th. 1.1}}

==Extension of traces==

The classical [[Trace operator|trace theory]] states that any Sobolev map <math>u \in W^{1, p} (M, N)</math> has a trace <math>Tu \in W^{1 - 1/p, p} (\partial M, N)</math> and that when <math>N = \mathbb{R}</math>, the trace operator is onto. The proof of the surjectivity being based on an averaging argument, the result does not readily extend to Sobolev mappings.
The trace operator is known to be onto when <math>\pi_{1} (N) \simeq \dotsb \pi_{\lfloor p - 1\rfloor}(N) \simeq \{0\}</math><ref name="Hardt_Lin_1987">{{cite journal |last1=Hardt |first1=Robert |last2=Lin |first2=Fang-Hua |title=Mappings minimizing the L<sup>p</sup> norm of the gradient |journal=Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics |date=September 1987 |volume=40 |issue=5 |pages=555–588 |doi=10.1002/cpa.3160400503}}</ref> or when <math>p\ge 3</math>, <math>\pi_{1} (N)</math> is finite and <math>\pi_{2} (N) \simeq \dotsb \pi_{\lfloor p - 1\rfloor}(N) \simeq \{0\}</math>.<ref name="Mironescu_VanSchaftingen_2021">{{cite journal |last1=Mironescu |first1=Petru |last2=Van Schaftingen |first2=Jean |title=Trace theory for Sobolev mappings into a manifold |journal=Annales de la Faculté des Sciences de Toulouse: Mathématiques |date=9 July 2021 |volume=30 |issue=2 |pages=281–299|arxiv=2001.02226|doi=10.5802/afst.1675|s2cid=210023485 }}</ref> The surjectivity of the trace operator fails if <math>\pi_{\lfloor p - 1\rfloor} (N)\not \simeq \{0\}</math> <ref name="Hardt_Lin_1987" /><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bethuel |first1=Fabrice |last2=Demengel |first2=Françoise |title=Extensions for Sobolev mappings between manifolds |journal=Calculus of Variations and Partial Differential Equations |date=October 1995 |volume=3 |issue=4 |pages=475–491 |doi=10.1007/BF01187897|s2cid=121749565 }}</ref> or if <math>\pi_{\ell} (N)</math> is infinite for some <math>\ell \in \{1, \dotsc, \lfloor p - 1\rfloor\}</math>.<ref name="Mironescu_VanSchaftingen_2021"/><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bethuel |first1=Fabrice |title=A new obstruction to the extension problem for Sobolev maps between manifolds |journal=Journal of Fixed Point Theory and Applications |date=March 2014 |volume=15 |issue=1 |pages=155–183 |doi=10.1007/s11784-014-0185-0|arxiv=1402.4614 |s2cid=119614310 }}</ref>

==Lifting==

Given a [[covering map]] <math>\pi : \tilde{N} \to N</math>, the lifting problem asks whether any map <math>u \in W^{s, p} (M, N)</math> can be written as <math>u = \pi \circ \tilde{u}</math> for some <math>\tilde{u} \in W^{s, p} (M, \tilde{N})</math>, as it is the case for continuous or smooth <math>u</math> and <math>\tilde{u}</math> when <math>M</math> is [[Simply connected space|simply-connected]] in the [[Covering space#Lifting property|classical lifting theory]].
If the domain <math>M</math> is simply connected, any map <math>u \in W^{s, p} (M, N)</math> can be written as <math>u = \pi \circ \tilde{u}</math> for some <math>\tilde{u} \in W^{s, p} (M, N)</math>
when <math>sp \ge \dim M</math>,<ref name="Bourgain_Brezis_Mironescu_2001">
{{cite journal |last1=Bourgain |first1=Jean |authorlink1=Jean Bourgain |last2=Brezis |first2=Haim |authorlink2=Haïm Brezis |last3=Mironescu |first3=Petru |title=Lifting in Sobolev spaces |journal=[[Journal d'Analyse Mathématique]] |date=December 2000 |volume=80 |issue=1 |pages=37–86 |doi=10.1007/BF02791533 |doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name="Bethuel_Chiron_2007">{{cite journal |last1=Bethuel |first1=Fabrice |last2=Chiron |first2=David |title=Some questions related to the lifting problem in Sobolev spaces |journal=Contemporary Mathematics |date=2007 |volume=446 |pages=125–152 |doi=10.1090/conm/446/08628|isbn=9780821841907 }}</ref> when <math>s\ge 1</math> and <math>2 \le sp <\dim M</math><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bethuel |first1=Fabrice |last2=Zheng |first2=Xiaomin |title=Density of smooth functions between two manifolds in Sobolev spaces |journal=Journal of Functional Analysis |date=September 1988 |volume=80 |issue=1 |pages=60–75 |doi=10.1016/0022-1236(88)90065-1|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name="Bethuel_Chiron_2007" />
and when <math>N</math> is compact, <math>0 < s <1</math> and <math>2 \le sp <\dim M</math>.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Mironescu |first1=Petru |last2=Van Schaftingen |first2=Jean |title=Lifting in compact covering spaces for fractional Sobolev mappings |journal=Analysis & PDE |date=7 September 2021 |volume=14 |issue=6 |pages=1851–1871 |arxiv=1907.01373|doi=10.2140/apde.2021.14.1851|s2cid=195776361 }}</ref>
There is a topological obstruction to the lifting when <math>sp < 2 </math> and an analytical obstruction when <math>1 \le sp < \dim M</math>.<ref name="Bourgain_Brezis_Mironescu_2001"/><ref name="Bethuel_Chiron_2007"/>
